Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler version of the same problem. Each recursive function needs a *base case*, which is a condition where it stops calling itself to avoid going on forever. You can think of it like looking in two mirrors facing each other: the image repeats many times, but you decide at some point to stop looking further. In programming, recursion is often used to work with nested structures like folders inside folders or to break big problems into smaller identical steps.
